description.narrative:
Insatsen omfattar ett programstöd till Världshälsoorganisationen (WHO) för genomförandet av Partnership for Maternal, Newborn & Child Health's (PMNCH) strategi 2026–2030 inom ramen för Strategi för Sveriges utvecklingssamarbete för hälsa samt sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter, 2025–2029.
PMNCH är ett WHO-värdpartnerskap med över 1 400 medlemsorganisationer från regeringar, civilsamhälle, ungdomsorganisationer, multilaterala organisationer, akademi och privat sektor. Partnerskapet bedöms ha en unik roll i den globala hälsoarkitekturen genom sin förmåga att samla olika aktörer för gemensamt påverkansarbete, ansvarsutkrävande och mobilisering för kvinnors, barns och ungdomars hälsa och välbefinnande, inklusive sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR).
Insatsen syftar till att stärka politiskt påverkansarbete, ansvarsutkrävande, hållbar finansiering, rättighetsbaserad lagstiftning och policyutveckling samt multisektoriella partnerskap för kvinnors, barns och ungdomars hälsa och välbefinnande

The contribution constitutes a programme support through the World Health Organization (WHO) to the Partnership for Maternal, Newborn & Child Health (PMNCH) for the period 2026–2029. PMNCH is a WHO-hosted partnership comprising more than 1,400 member organizations from governments, civil society, youth organizations, multilateral organizations, academia and the private sector. PMNCH is assessed to be a strategically important actor within the global health architecture and one of the few platforms that brings together a broad range of stakeholders to advance advocacy, accountability and mobilization for the health and well-being of women, children and adolescents, including sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR).
The intervention aims to contribute to the implementation of PMNCH’s 2026–2030 Strategy through five workstreams focusing on political advocacy, country-level accountability, sustainable financing, rights-based laws and policy development, multisectoral partnerships, and countering misinformation and disinformation.

This initiative contains five workstreams for 20262029, all aligned with PMNCHs 20262030 Strategy and 20262027 Workplan. The intervention focuses on evidence-based strategies to strengthen advocacy, accountability, financing and multi-stakeholder action for womens, childrens and adolescents health (WCAH), with a particular emphasis on sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR).
The five workstreams are:
1. Support high-level political advocacy with a focus on SRHR and sustainable financing. 2. Catalyse acceleration and foster accountability at country level. 3. Build multisectoral alliances, including with the private sector, to scale low-cost innovations for WCAH. 4. Advance progressive laws and policies and conduct rights-based advocacy. 5. Confront mis- and dis-information and enhance digital communication.
Targets and expected impacts for each workstream are outlined below.
Workstream 1: Support high-level political advocacy with a focus on SRHR and sustainable financing
Targets
By the end of 2029, 6 global, regional or national statements or resolutions explicitly referencing WCAH and SRHR priorities. By the end of 2029, 10 speeches, op-eds or media appearances publicly championing WCAH and SRHR by Global Leaders Network members and/or parliamentarians. By the end of 2029, 6 domestic resource mobilisation (DRM) and/or innovative financing webinars or events conducted to strengthen partner capacity.
Expected impact
WCAH and SRHR remain prominent priorities in global and regional policy processes. SRHR is protected and advanced within evolving global health and UN reform discussions. Increased political commitment and stronger capacity for domestic resource mobilisation contribute to more sustainable financing for WCAH and SRHR.
Workstream 2: Catalyse acceleration and foster accountability at country level
Targets
By the end of 2029, 5 CAAP countries supported to adopt costed budget plans with WCAH and SRHR investment cases. By the end of 2029, 4 youth or citizen hearings and social accountability sessions conducted. By the end of 2029, 6 peer-learning exchanges organised between CAAP implementing partners.
Expected impact
Improved translation of political commitments into budget allocations and implementation.
Strengthened accountability for WCAH and SRHR commitments at national and sub-national levels.
Enhanced capacity of national partners to advocate for policy change, financing and implementation.
Workstream 3: Build multisectoral alliances, including with the private sector, to scale low-cost innovations for WCAH
Targets
By the end of 2026, 2 convenings of public, private and other stakeholders to identify priorities for scaling low-cost innovations for WCAH.
By the end of 2027, a roadmap for scaling low-cost innovations agreed with participation from private sector actors, including Swedish actors.
Targets for 20282029 to be developed based on the final roadmap.
Expected impact
Stronger multisectoral collaboration supports the adoption and scale-up of affordable innovations for WCAH.
Improved access to services, technologies and commodities that contribute to reduced preventable morbidity and mortality among women, children and adolescents.
Workstream 4: Advance progressive laws and policies and conduct rights-based advocacy
Targets
By the end of 2029, 8 joint advocacy actions undertaken by the PMNCH-led SRHR Advocacy Coalition and/or the Global South Coalition on SRHR and Development Justice. By the end of 2029, 5 regional and/or global dialogues organised to advance rights-based policy and legal frameworks. By the end of 2029, support provided to SRHR-related legal and policy processes in at least 3 African countries. By the end of 2029, 100 parliamentarians trained to support progressive legislation for SRHR and WCAH.
Expected impact
Stronger alignment and coherence of advocacy efforts in support of SRHR. More enabling legal and policy environments for WCAH and SRHR at national, regional and global levels. Increased capacity of political leaders and institutions to advance rights-based legislation and policies.
Workstream 5: Confront mis- and dis-information and enhance digital communication
Targets
By 2026, launch of the PMNCH FactCheck platform and progressive uptake by partners during 2027-2029. By 2029, 4 capacity-building workshops conducted to strengthen digital advocacy capacity among CAAP partners.
Expected impact
Increased access to and use of evidence-based information on WCAH and SRHR. Strengthened capacity of partners to counter misinformation and engage effectively in digital advocacy. A stronger enabling environment for evidence-based policy and advocacy on WCAH, SRHR and adolescent health and well-being.
The intervention is currently in its initial phase. Results will be reported no earlier than 2027.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
